ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement screening against the Canadian Consolidated Sanctions List published by Global Affairs Canada, the Special Economic Measures Act regulations, the OFAC SDN List for any USD-denominated transactions, the UN Security Council 1267/1988 and 2231 sanctions lists, and UK/EU consolidated equivalents; mandatory identification and verification of beneficial ownership under FINTRAC rules; enhanced due diligence required for foreign politically exposed persons, domestic politically exposed persons, and heads of international organizations, including their family members and close associates; adverse-media monitoring and negative news review applied to all identified UBOs and directors before name clearance is lodged.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry operated by Service Alberta; NUANS name search and name reservation are processed in real time through accredited Registry Agents, with the official online portal at albertaregistries.ca and corporate search via authorized service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed using Latin-alphabet characters in English or French and must include a mandatory legal element such as Limited, Ltee, Corporation, Corp., Incorporated or Inc.; non-Latin scripts used in cross-border branding must be transliterated into Roman characters for the NUANS examination; confusion screening covers phonetic and homophonic equivalents, and a separate unregistered trade name in Chinese characters does not form part of the registered corporate name unless romanized and approved
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Loan, Insurance, Assurance, Financial (regulated financial services indicators requiring charter or ministerial consent)
University, College, Institute, Academy (post-secondary education designations requiring accreditation authorization)
Royal, Queen, King, Crown, Federal, Government, or any word implying Crown patronage or government affiliation
Optician, Dispensing Optician, Optometrist, Ophthalmologist (regulated health profession titles restricted to licensed practitioners under Alberta health legislation)
Words that are grossly offensive or scandalous within the meaning of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
Use of Canada as a leading or dominant element without federal consent or the required continuity with a federal predecessor
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant or its authorized registry agent may file a written reconsideration request with the Director of Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, within 30 days of the refusal, attaching supporting evidence such as a written consent from the conflicting nameholder, a registered trademark certificate, or a revised NUANS report; if the Director maintains the refusal, the applicant may commence judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta by originating application, which must be filed within six months of the final administrative decision, pursuant to the Alberta Rules of Court and the Judicature Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this non-regulated wholesale distribution industry: the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) requires a registered office continuously maintained within Alberta as the address for service of process and statutory records; a virtual-office or registered-agent address is accepted by the Alberta Corporate Registry, provided it is a genuine serviceable location, but banks and the Canada Revenue Agency will expect meaningful commercial substance, including board decision-making, books and records, and management control within Canada for international wholesale operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-trivial; estimated 8-12% probability within the first 24 months. Triggers include CRA audit selection, GST/HST verification, municipal business licence inspection if any physical warehouse premise is opened in Calgary or Edmonton, and targeted anti-money-laundering supervision; unannounced registry inspections of the corporate premises are not a standard Alberta Corporate Registry practice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), ss 6-10 (Articles and Certificate of Incorporation), s 11 (Corporate Name), s 14 (Directors), ss 103-104 (Registered Office and Records); ABCA Regulations, AR 276/2000, Form 1
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Corporate Registrations Division, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation — Alberta Corporate Registry Form 1 (ABCA), filed online through the Registry Connect portal or submitted through an authorized Registry Agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital, no escrow deposit, and no reserve fund requirement under the ABCA. Authorized capital is set out in the Articles and shares are issued for such consideration as the Board determines, provided each share is fully paid at the time of issue. At least one director is required, and a majority of ABCA directors must be resident Canadians unless a Statutory Exemption Order applies. Non-resident ownership of shares is unrestricted. The online incorporation filing fee is CAD 200, equivalent to approximately USD 148 at customary conversion.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS — Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, it is RESOLVED: 1. The Incorporator's subscription for 10,000 Common Shares at CAD $0.10 per share is accepted and the shares are issued fully paid. 2. The Corporation's registered office is fixed at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation. 3. The proposed By-Law No. 1, as presented, is unanimously adopted. 4. John Smith is appointed Chief Executive Officer, Jane Doe is appointed Secretary-Treasurer; each shall hold office until removed by the Board. 5. The officers are authorized to open bank accounts and execute warehousing, distribution and international trade contracts in the ordinary course. 6. All formation documents and actions of the Incorporator are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Corporate Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized Registry Agent or the online Registry Connect portal (Service Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a premium NUANS name search request to obtain the Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search report for the proposed corporate name, which must include a distinctive element and a legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', or 'Ltee'. File a corporate name reservation to hold the approved name for 90 days. Provide the complete postal and street address details and confirm the selected jurisdiction is Alberta.
required_dossiers: NUANS premium name search report
Corporate name reservation request form
Written consent or waiver for any distinctive or sensitive word used in the name, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of indistinctiveness or confusing similarity, obtain a fresh NUANS report under an amended name and re-file the reservation. Where the desired name is unavailable, request the Director of Corporate Registries to exercise discretionary approval under ABCA s 11(2).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Online Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Corporate Registrations Division, Service Alberta (Registry Connect portal); in-person filing at authorized Registry Agents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) stating the corporate name, registered office address within Alberta, share classes and maximum authorized shares, special rights and restrictions attached to such shares, the number of first directors, and any restrictions on share transfers. Executed by the incorporator through electronic signature. Attach the certified NUANS report, submit via Registry Connect, and pay the CAD 200 online filing fee by credit card or pre-authorized debit.
required_dossiers: Certified NUANS name search report dated within 90 days of filing
Alberta Articles of Incorporation Form 1 duly executed
Consent to Act as First Director signed by each initial director
Registered office street address and municipal location
Electronic payment confirmation for the CAD 200 filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry examiner issues a deficiency notice or Request for Further Information, cure the stated defect by amending the Articles or by submitting an explanatory statutory declaration, then electronically refile. Disputes concerning completeness or eligibility may be appealed to the Registrar for a written ruling under ABCA s 8(2).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar endorses and files the Articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation electronically, together with the Corporate Access Number. Verify the corporation's full legal name, registered office, director count, and share terms exactly as reflected in the certificate. Archive the system-generated certificate and endorsed Articles in the permanent corporate records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (system-issued electronic record)
Endorsed Articles of Incorporation
Corporate Access Number notice of confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains clerical errors or fails to match the approved Articles, apply for a correction under the ABCA certificate correction procedure, supported by a statutory declaration of the incorporator, and obtain a revised certificate with retroactive effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Adoption of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation; corporate minute book maintained at the Alberta registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting of the incorporator and first directors, or execute a written resolution in lieu of meeting under ABCA s 104. Adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution accepting the share subscription, fixing the registered office, approving By-Law No. 1, appointing the Chief Executive Officer and Secretary-Treasurer, and ratifying all pre-incorporation acts. Issue share certificates against the fully paid consideration and complete the securities register, directors register, and transfer ledger.
required_dossiers: Written First Board Resolution (pro-forma resolution)
By-Law No. 1 general operating by-law
Consent to Act as Director and signed oaths of office
Share certificate book, securities register, and share transfer ledger
Registered office landlord consent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director withdraws consent or quorum is lost, appoint a substitute director by written resolution and file the Director Change form with the Corporate Registry within 15 days. Re-issue any defective share certificate in compliance with ABCA s 44 and re-execute the subscription to ensure fully paid status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Alberta Tax and WCB Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration online portal and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration; Alberta Workers' Compensation Board (WCB-Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Corporate Access Number to register for the 15-digit CRA Business Number and open federal accounts for GST/HST, corporate income tax, payroll deductions for future employees, and the Import/Export RM account required for international optical-frame transactions. Register with the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration for Alberta corporate income tax at the general rate of 8% or the small business rate of 2%, and register with WCB-Alberta as an employer for workers' compensation coverage.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Number
CRA Business Number registration application
Registered office address and principal place of business
Business activity description under NAICS 423460 / ISIC 4646
Annual revenue projection for GST/HST threshold determination
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries name or address data, call the CRA Business Enquiries line at 1-800-959-5525 and submit corrected information. If WCB-Alberta assigns an incorrect industry classification, file a reclassification request describing optical-frame wholesale distribution for assessment-rate adjustment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence, Safety Codes, and Environmental Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary Business Licensing or City of Edmonton Corporate Business Licensing; Alberta Safety Codes Council; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the municipal business licence application for 'Wholesale Trade — Optical Frames Storage and Distribution', attaching the lease or ownership title evidencing compliant zoning, the Certificate of Incorporation, and the CRA Business Number. Obtain the Safety Codes occupant load and fire code inspection clearance for the warehouse premises. Submit notice to Alberta Environment and Protected Areas only where municipal development permitting thresholds are crossed; maintain waste, packaging, and recycling documentation under the provincial recycling regime.
required_dossiers: Municipal Business Licence application and fee
Certificate of Incorporation and CRA Business Number
Lease agreement or proof of premises ownership with zoning compliance
Alberta Fire Code inspection checklist and occupancy certificate
WCB-Alberta registration number
Waste and packaging recycling records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses the licence for zoning or building-code breaches, apply for a discretionary development permit or variance, or relocate the distribution facility to a conforming industrial or warehousing zone. If the Fire Marshal identifies deficiencies, remediate egress, suppression, or storage configuration matters and re-inspect.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Business Licensing departments of the City of Calgary and City of Edmonton; provincial occupational oversight by Alberta Labour and Immigration — Occupational Health and Safety; environmental authority retained by Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence — Wholesale Trade of Optical Eyewear Frames (NAICS 423460 / ISIC 4646), supplemented by Alberta Fire Code occupancy clearance and WCB-Alberta registration; no federal or provincial industry-specific manufacturing licence is applicable to optical-frame wholesale distribution

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas — Environmental Assessment and Approvals Division; municipal drainage and development permit authority of the City of Calgary or City of Edmonton
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Full EIA not mandatory: wholesale warehousing and distribution of acetate eyeglass frames is not listed among mandatory or self-assessed activities under the Environmental Assessment (Mandatory and Exempt Activities) Regulation, AR 111/1993. Only routine municipal development and stormwater registration applies; no provincial environmental approval is required for storage-only premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions, or industrial effluent streams arise from optical-frame distribution; sanitary sewage must comply with municipal sewer use by-laws, typically BOD ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.5. HVAC refrigerant management must follow applicable ozone-depleting substance codes. Waste and packaging handling must comply with Alberta recycling regulations including AR 51/2017 for electronic waste and municipal packaging and printed paper programs; zero hazardous-waste generation is expected from acetate and plastic frame storage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Alberta Fire Code fire safety inspection, egress clearance, and fire department access certification; structural occupancy approval under Division B, Part 3 of the Alberta Building Code issued by Safety Codes Council-accredited municipal inspectors; Occupational Health and Safety clearance under Alberta OHS covering hazard assessment, materials handling, lifting controls, and emergency planning; mandatory WCB-Alberta employer registration and annual payroll reporting for workers' compensation coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must obtain a Canada Business Number (BN) to administer GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts. For a non-resident corporation, the standard procedure is to complete Form RC1, 'Request for a Business Number and Tax Accounts', and submit it by mail, fax, or through CRA's online 'Register and Open a Business Account' service. Alternatively, a corporation incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act or an Alberta provincial statute may request registration of tax accounts during the incorporation process. The foreign entity must provide proof of legal existence (certificate of incorporation from its home jurisdiction), a registered office address in its home jurisdiction, and the name and address of a Canadian contact (e.g., counsel, accountant, or bank branch) where applicable. If the entity has no permanent establishment, the CRA typically requires a non-resident tax representative or an authorization arrangement. GST/HST registration is mandatory when the non-resident makes taxable supplies in Canada and is not a small supplier; otherwise, the entity may still register voluntarily to claim input tax credits or to comply with export zero-rating documentation expectations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not offer the U.S.-style 'check-the-box' election. For a Canadian business corporation, the relevant statutory elections include: (i) the closely related corporations election under subsection 128(1) of the Excise Tax Act, which permits related corporations to make certain otherwise-taxable supplies non-taxable for GST/HST; (ii) the non-resident corporation election under section 216 of the Income Tax Act, allowing a non-resident to file a Canadian income tax return and elect to compute tax on certain Canadian-source rental income as if the activity were a separate business; (iii) the branch tax election under section 219 of the Income Tax Act, deeming a non-resident corporation to be operating a Canadian branch; and (iv) provisions under sections 18.4 to 18.7 of the Income Tax Act that impose hybrid mismatch re-characterization, but no elective opt-out is available for hybrid mismatch rules. Provincial-level elections in Alberta are absent because Alberta levies no separate corporate capital tax or provincial sales tax, but Alberta corporate income tax registration is effected through the CRA corporate payments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) administered under the Excise Tax Act; Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST, with no provincial sales tax and no HST portion.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (exclusive of zero-rated exports) over any single calendar quarter or over a trailing twelve-month period; non-resident persons who are not small suppliers and who carry on business in Canada must register. Importers and service providers with no physical presence also trigger mandatory GST/HST registration when the $30,000 threshold is exceeded, unless their only Canadian supplies are zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping, or pre-authorization API for invoices. Electronic invoicing is legally permitted and CRA's record-keeping requirements allow EDI or PDF invoices; no specific 'clearance' step is required. Alberta's administrative practice follows the federal e-invoicing regime, and there is no provincial mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: To claim 0% GST/HST on exported ophthalmic eyewear frames, the supplier must be a registrant who, in the course of a commercial activity, exports goods and meets the evidential requirements of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. The goods must be delivered to a location outside Canada and leave Canada within a reasonable time after the sale; for a typical wholesale shipment, CRA expects export to occur within 60 to 90 days. Services supplied in connection with the goods (e.g., export booking services) are zero-rated only if the services are 'exported' to a non-resident. The supplier must prove that the goods were exported by retaining, among other records, the export declaration and a bill of lading showing a Canadian origin and a foreign destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration (B13A) filed electronically via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CAES) or the annual export report in the retailer's database
Commercial invoice describing the acetate eyeglass frames, HS classification (ISIC 4646 corresponds to NAICS 423460), and shipment quantities
Bill of lading (original or electronic) or air waybill showing departure from Canada and delivery to the non-resident buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank statement showing receipt of foreign-currency payment (commonly requested by CRA as supporting evidence, although not an explicit GST/HST statutory document)
Packing list evidencing the shipped contents
Purchase order or export contract with the non-resident customer identifying the final destination country
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If CRA determines that goods were not in fact exported, the zero-rated treatment is reversed and the supply becomes taxable at 5% GST in Alberta. Assessments may be reopened retroactively within four years of the date of assessment, or seven years if a misrepresentation attributable to carelessness, negligence, or willful attempt to evade tax is established. Penalties include the false-statement penalty under section 285.1 of the Excise Tax Act, which is generally 25% of the net tax misstatement for knowingly or grossly negligent filings, plus interest and the potential denial of input tax credits previously claimed. Export refunds already received may be clawed back with interest, and further penalties under the Income Tax Act can apply if the export arrangement was mischaracterized to reduce income.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — central bank, sole issuer of Canadian bank notes, operator of the Lynx high-value settlement system, and supervisor of retail payment service providers under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA). The Department of Finance Canada (Minister of Finance) administers the Exchange Fund Account and foreign exchange reserve policy; OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) licenses and supervises federally chartered Schedule I banks; FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) enforces cross-border currency reporting and electronic funds transfer monitoring under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); ISED (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) administers the Investment Canada Act for inbound non-Canadian investment. Canada maintains no exchange-control authority and imposes no pre-approval, licence, quota, or central-bank permit for current-account or capital-account payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations since 1952; the Canadian Dollar (CAD) floats freely, and both current-account and capital-account transactions are unrestricted. There are no statutory barriers to profit remittance: a solvent Alberta business corporation may pay dividends, repay shareholder loans, and pay interest/royalties without ministerial or central-bank consent. The only remittance costs are fiscal: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax at 25% (statutory), reduced under income tax treaties (e.g., dividends generally 5% where the beneficial owner is a treaty-resident company holding at least 10% of the voting shares; otherwise 15%; arm's-length interest is generally exempt from Part XIII; related-party interest and royalties attract treaty-reduced rates). Practical hurdles are compliance-driven, not exchange-control-driven: the paying bank requires board resolutions, source-of-funds proof, and a valid SWIFT purpose description; every EFT of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC. Repatriation of capital and dividends is immediate and unrestricted once the bank's compliance conditions are satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None exist. Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no statutory retention timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. An Alberta wholesale distributor may retain 100% of foreign-currency export proceeds indefinitely, hold USD/EUR/CNH in domestic or offshore accounts, and convert them in the spot market at any time. The only binding requirements are reporting-based: physical import/export of currency or monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more must be declared to the Canada Border Services Agency under the Cross-Border Currency and Monetary Instruments Reporting Regulations (PCMLTFA); financial institutions must record and report international EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC; and the corporation must maintain export invoices, customs declarations, and settlement evidence to satisfy banking AML monitoring and CRA audit requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Business Corporations Act (Alberta), s. 260.1; Corporations Information Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta / registered agents)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation or amalgamation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fee CAD 40; continued default may trigger Registrar's notice and administrative strike-off/cancellation of the corporation, with loss of limited liability status and vesting of corporate assets in the Crown upon dissolution; directors may incur personal liability for liabilities arising after default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (applicable only if the entity is a CBCA federal corporation; the provincial Alberta entity files the Alberta Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or continuance each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fee CAD 50; failure to file for one year may lead to administrative dissolution under CBCA s. 212 after warning letters; reinstatement requires additional filings and fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal corporate income tax and capital tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the end of the taxation year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, due June 30 of the following calendar year (Income Tax Act s. 150(1))
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per complete month of delinquency (maximum 12 months); prescribed interest compounded daily on unpaid tax and penalties; possible arbitrary assessment under s. 152(7); loss of carry-back refunds; repeat late filing triggers a 10% penalty; directors may be liable for unremitted source deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AT1 Alberta Corporate Tax Return (Alberta provincial corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA); return is filed jointly through the Canada Revenue Agency under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the end of the taxation year, aligned with the federal T2 due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing, late-payment and instalment penalties substantially equivalent to the federal T2 regime; prescribed interest accrues daily on deficient amounts; Alberta may pursue collection against Alberta-based assets and freeze registry clearances after sustained non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (annual filing for qualifying registrants with total annual worldwide revenues not exceeding CAD 1.5 million; otherwise quarterly or monthly remittances apply)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers: no later than 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; quarterly filers: no later than 1 month after the end of each reporting period (Excise Tax Act s. 228)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the amount owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months; prescribed daily interest on unpaid net tax; failure to charge or remit GST/HST attracts penalties and, in the case of willful evasion, prosecution; directors may be personally assessed for unremitted GST/HST under s. 323 Excise Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ISC Register Review and Confirmation (Register of Individuals with Significant Control)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Beneficial Ownership Transparency Registry; on-site corporate records maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Register maintained continuously and updated within 15 days of any change; annual confirmation submitted with the Alberta Annual Return within the 60-day anniversary filing window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain, correct or produce the ISC register exposes the corporation, directors and officers to fines up to CAD 1,000 per day and up to CAD 10,000 on summary conviction under s. 164.5(4); knowingly suppressing ISC information is an offence; incomplete annual return certification additionally exposes the corporation to strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), an auditor must be appointed at each annual meeting unless the corporation is a non-distributing private corporation and every shareholder, including every shareholder not entitled to vote, has waived the audit in writing for the year (s. 154); the ABCA imposes no revenue or asset threshold for the private-corporation waiver. Where no waiver is obtained, audited financial statements must be presented to the shareholders. The CRA may require an auditor's report under the Income Tax Act where financial statements are inadequate or upon ministerial demand; commercial lenders financing the eyewear wholesale operation will typically impose an independent audit covenant in credit agreements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook – IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; a private Alberta wholesale corporation may elect Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), Part II, or IFRS; financial statements must be prepared on an accrual basis and must substantiate the T2, AT1 and GST/HST filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under ABCA s. 164.1, the corporation must identify and record every individual with significant control, defined as any person owning or controlling, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of the voting shares or of shares representing 25% or more of the fair market value, or any person with actual control over the corporation. Any share transfer in the wholesale vehicle must be reviewed; the register must be updated within 15 days of a change and confirmed as accurate, complete and current during the annual return cycle. Authorized inspection bodies may access the register without notice, and ISC data is collected through Alberta's Corporate Registry for the Beneficial Ownership Transparency Registry (BOTR) for law enforcement and statutory use.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: ISC Register (Register of Individuals with Significant Control – Alberta BCA s. 164.1)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110–370 (CAD 150–500) per year for a registered office and provincial registered agent in Alberta; bundled corporate secretarial packages range from USD 350–900 per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–20,000 (CAD 7,000–27,000) for a certified independent audit of a small wholesale distribution corporation holding inventory and foreign-supplier records; reviewed financial statements acceptable to creditors typically range from USD 2,500–6,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined (15% federal + 8% Alberta) for a general business corporation; reduced combined rate of 11% applies to qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Preferential deductions include the federal small business deduction for CCPCs, the federal general rate reduction, the scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) investment tax credit, and the foreign tax credit. Alberta imposes no provincial capital tax or general payroll tax on corporations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically through a CRA-certified EFILE/NETFILE service provider or via the 'My Business Account' portal. Alberta corporate tax is administered by the CRA under the collection agreement, so a single federal-provincial T2 return is compulsory.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within 6 months after the corporation’s fiscal year-end. The balance of tax owing is generally due 2 months after year-end (3 months for CCPCs claiming the small business deduction).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number (BN), incorporation date, jurisdiction, fiscal year-end, and mailing address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the full legal name and address of each non-resident shareholder; attach a Canada Revenue Agency trust analysis if >50% foreign-owned; ensure all corporate records are in English.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before taxes per financial statements, reconciled with tax adjustments for non-deductible expenses, deductible allowances, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the arm's-length nature of all cross-border purchases and sales of acetate eyeglass frames; apply the selected OECD methodology consistently with the functional analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting prior-year non-capital losses (20-year carryforward, 3-year carryback) and capital loss restrictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Schedule 9 to evidence loss carryforwards. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Alberta through a permanent establishment must allocate income to Canada under the income tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta provincial corporate income tax at 8% of taxable income allocated to Alberta.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a corporation resident in Canada, taxable income is the same; for a non-resident with a permanent establishment, allocate taxable income using the formulary rules of the Canada-Alberta agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of federal tax before credits: 38% basic rate less 10% provincial abatement less 13% general rate reduction (yielding 15%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the general rate reduction in full for eligible business income; do not claim the small business deduction unless the corporation is a CCPC and shares are not listed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of delinquency, up to 12 months (10% plus 2% per month if the failure was knowingly made or under gross negligence). Interest at prescribed rates is charged on late payments. A failure to respond to a CRA demand may trigger a daily $25 penalty.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding, the non-resident shareholder must complete CRA Form NR301 (Statement of Entitlement to Treaty Benefits) or Form NR302/NR303 where applicable, and provide a certificate of residence from the treaty jurisdiction. The paying corporation must withhold and remit the reduced rate on the basis of that documentation. If withholding was excessive, the recipient may file a NR7 application for refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rate on interest and royalties to non-residents is 25%. Under the Canada–US tax treaty, interest is generally exempt from Canadian withholding tax and royalties are 10% (0% for certain copyright royalties). Other treaties may reduce or eliminate these rates; a proper treaty certificate must be in place before the payment is made.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada imposes no statutory Local File/Master File threshold; however, transfer-pricing penalty under s.247(3) may apply when the aggregate value of specified cross-border transactions exceeds CAD 5 million and documentation is not produced within 90 days of a CRA request. Country-by-country reporting is mandatory for multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of CAD 750 million or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain separate Economic Substance Regulations. The CRA applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) to deny tax benefits from transactions lacking bona fide economic substance, and the statutory transfer-pricing rules require the pricing to correspond to the substance of the transaction. A shell company or conduit may be re-characterized and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – False statements or willful misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misstating gross income, inflating deductions, using undisclosed foreign bank accounts, creating fictitious suppliers, or deliberately omitting revenue from wholesale eyeglass frame exports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty equal to 50% of the tax evaded (Income Tax Act s.163), plus interest and the unpaid tax. Criminal conviction under the Criminal Code s.380 may trigger a fine of up to 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment for up to 5 years; provincial penalties also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable under s.227.1 for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST; if they participated in or consented to the evasion, they can be assessed the civil penalty and may be criminally prosecuted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Conduit Abuse and Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a nominal Canadian corporation with no real employees or commercial activity, used solely to route profits to a low-tax jurisdiction via inflated royalty, interest, or management-fee payments to a non-resident affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA may disregard the transaction under GAAR, recharacterize the payments as dividends, and apply a 25% withholding tax. A gross-negligence penalty of 10% of the misreported amount (s.163.2) and interest may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false tax returns or authorize the conduit arrangement may be personally liable for penalties and the unremitted withholding tax; they are exposed to criminal prosecution for conspiracy to evade tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain basic AML entry records, accepting Swift_TT or Platform_Pay payments without implementing a compliance regime, or processing transactions involving sanctioned persons or proceeds of crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: False or incomplete reports under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act attract administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation; criminal offence convictions can result in fines of up to CAD 2,000,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly fail to implement required AML controls can be personally fined and imprisoned; the Crown can impose director liability for the corporation’s AML obligations if the director had operational authority.
